utterances.text: Can you recall how exactly you received the order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. Probably over the communication system.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who did that second order come from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was from our superior officer, commander.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you assemble before you set out to carry out your second task?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: In the vicinity of the Yellow Bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you mentioned a name from whom the order came, the superior officer. Could you please repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rade Cuturic, also known as Oficir. Oficir was his nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How were you transported to the area where you were supposed to carry out your second order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, we had a bus at our disposal as well as two military vehicles, 110 and 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, to the best of your recollection, what was that second order that you received from Rade Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The order was that we would be deployed to the place called Kravica, to provide security for the Bratunac-Konjevic Polje road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you told what the reason was, why you had to secure that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why were you charged with securing this specific road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The reason was that a large group of armed Muslims was heading from Srebrenica and there was a risk that the road might be cut off, meaning the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road. There was a possibility that the Muslim forces might try to cut off the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more question, Your Honour, if I may, and then I will stop before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the right-hand side of the road facing Konjevic Polje was the rear side of the Serbian villages in the area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Kravica and some other villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Based on your experience of an individual who had been in the war for a couple of years by then, was this a legitimate task to be given to your unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it's our time for the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take a break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, can you please tell the Trial Chamber, in your best recollection, what the time of day was when you came to the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From what I can remember, I think it was perhaps in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were taking up the position, did you notice if there were any other police or military formations there already?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, not as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just briefly tell us, because you already said that in the statement, in relation to the Kravica warehouse, who was the closest in the disposition that you had at that particular time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were deployed according to platoons. That was the disposition. So I don't know if it was the 1st, 2nd or the 3rd Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which of these three platoons was the closest to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was the 1st Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember if there were any members of the PJP units with you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the "Posebna Jedinica Policije," police unit from the Zvornik centre was with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember where that unit was deployed in relation to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: They were positioned along the road from Sandici to Konjevic Polje, that section.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time that day in the afternoon, did you see any military formation along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you stayed there the following night on that assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember but I think that we did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During that afternoon and night, did you have one single prisoner in the sector where you yourself were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that afternoon, that evening and night, there were any battles with the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember if there were any casualties among the PJP unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: One member of the PJP unit was killed in the Sandici sector. I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 65 ter 04082 in e-court, please? We will need to look at the second page of both the English and the B/C/S versions of the document. And while we are waiting for the document, Your Honours, I just want to say that this is a document that we refer to as Ljubomir Borovcanin's report for July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before I put the question to you about the document, what I would like to ask you first is this: Can you please tell us, if you know, Rade Cuturic, aka Oficir, who did he get the orders from that he conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I assume that he got it from his superior, either the brigade commander or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know, then, according to the principle of singleness of command and subordination, who they, in turn, would receive their orders from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this for the following reason: On page 2 that you can see in front of you, in the fifth paragraph, or the sixth paragraph, in the Borovcanin report, it states for the 12th of July, 1995, that he received an order from General Mladic to take one half of the men and the available equipment to that section in order to block the terrain and to fight the said formation. I'm asking you this first: Do you know that all the police units came to that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that at that time, in the area where you were, the road and Potocari, the Jahorina training centre unit was there too?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And at any point in time, did you have the opportunity to encounter members of the Jahorina training centre unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, not at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were the members of those units part of the police force?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who comprised that training centre, Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were fairly young guys. I don't know how they became members of the unit. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to hear the term about the presence of deserters in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think, as far as I can remember, there were these so-called deserters, that's what you called them, who were part of that unit. They were also in that unit from the training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the document that you have in front of you, it's the last paragraph in the English version, Your Honours, and Mr. Pepic, it's the paragraph above the phrase, "13th of July, 1995," it states, "along the road from Kravica, Sandici, Pervani, up to Hrcici [phoen], the SOP is deployed."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question and the witness his last two answers? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you please repeat your question and could the witness then repeat his answers?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, we will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question was: What does this abbreviation 2nd SP -- SOP means?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It probably means the 2nd Special Police Detachment, "Drugi Specijalni Odred Policije."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you a member of 2nd Detachment of the Special Police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm continuing to read: "And the first company of the PJP Zvornik with two tanks, a BOV 20/3, a Praga, and an MB platoon. During that night, there was fierce fighting. One policeman from the SM Bratunac was killed." And here I'm just going to ask you this: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber what the abbreviation SM Bratunac means?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: "Stanica milicije," most probably, "police station."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm continuing to read: "And there were several wounded. And then from N Kasaba up to K Polje, was covered by elements of the Protection Regiment." My question is: According to your best recollection, would this description of the deployment of the units along the road, Kravica-Konjevic Polje, agree with what you remember? Would that correspond to what your recollection was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would looking at this document jog your memory as to the fact that this happened on the 12th, in the evening, as you said?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 12th, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, so starting from the first assignment which was searching the terrain and then to the second assignment, to secure the road, at any point in time, did you see General Mladic at any of those locations?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to deal with the 13th. I would just like to ask, Your Honours, to look at this same document and then in the English version, only in the English version, could we move to page 3, this is the second paragraph which states -- the second paragraph, it says in the report: "Forces of the VRS mostly regrouped in order to go to Zepa." I'm asking you now if you recall whether, on the 13th, on the road that you are talking about, while carrying out your assignment to secure the road, did you ever see any members of the VRS there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please tell me, in your best recollection, at what point in time, if you did see that at all, did your unit have any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to rephrase the question, perhaps it's complex. On the 13th of July, so the following day, at any point in time did you see prisoners in the sector where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I personally did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you the term "Sandici meadow," "livada Sandici," would you be able to remember where that location was that I'm asking you about?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then I'm going to ask you this: Whether your position, your personal position, was between the Kravica warehouse and the Sandici meadow?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm asking you this because you said that at one point your commander, Rade Cuturic, came to you and said that a group of prisoners was going to pass down that road. Do you remember at which point in time, on the 13th of July, was this, according to your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Perhaps it was sometime in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you what was the number of the prisoners involved?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you who would be escorting these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you if they were to pass by in vehicles or on foot?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he said that they were to pass on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any reason why you should be apprehensive of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you leave the area before the prisoners were taken through?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did other members of the unit stay behind to perform the task that they were given earlier, i.e. to secure that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, if I remember well, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point in your statement you mention Zuti Most, Yellow Bridge. Is the Yellow Bridge the feature where you gathered on the 12th of July to set out to perform your task, securing the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is one such bridge in Potocari and there is also one in Kravica. It's yellow in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did Rade Cuturic take you in his vehicle directly to that bridge that you refer to as the Yellow Bridge?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you that that was to be the place where you would stop any traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you heard that at this location, and you referred to the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road, General Mladic and Ljubisa Borovcanin were present at some point in time. Who did you hear this from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I do remember that they were in the field around Srebrenica and around Bratunac, specifically in -- for the Kravica and Sandici areas, I didn't hear that they were there. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say location, you mean the area of Srebrenica and Bratunac; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point see General Mladic pass by on the 13th of July, pass by that particular road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, as far as I remember, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you, before you set out with Rade Cuturic, have occasion to see clashes and exchange of fire between the positions held by the 28th Division column and the police forces on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What sort of gunfire was it? Was it only infantry weapons, or was heavy -- were heavy weapons used?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, there was infantry weapons and mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At a certain point, having left you behind near the bridge, Rade Cuturic gave you the communication device that you referred to as a Motorola; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if that belonged to him or he took it off somebody else and kept his own communication device?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: He probably took it from somebody else. He had his own Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he explain to you in any detail what the reasons were as to why you should stop the flow of traffic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. The reason being that this should enable the prisoners to be escorted to the farming co-operative in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What is your best estimate, how long did you stay at the bridge after receiving this task from Rade Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: If I recall correctly, an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During that one hour, if you recall, was there unhindered flow of traffic along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is my next question, and please tell me to the best of your recollection: Did you first receive an order to stop the flow of traffic and only then heard heavy shooting that you described to the Prosecution, or was the sequence of events the other way around?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. I first received an order, and then there was gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your estimate, how much time passed from the point you received this order to stop the flow of traffic to the time when shooting started?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you came to learn that a member of your detachment was harmed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, when our commander came to see me, he was on his way to Bratunac, he told me briefly what had happened and that Krsto was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me take you one step back. Did you hear on your communication system in code anything that would indicate to you that someone from your unit came in harm's way?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. We had a code indicating that the -- one of our men was either wounded or killed. And the code name was "snala," s-n-a-l-a, meaning hair clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with the assistance of our dear Janet can we see a clip from 1447?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I use the -- it was still present on our screens, the last document, that is the Borovcanin report. Witness, could I ask you to read the last line before -- and we -- and that it's -- for you it is the last line of the page which is on the screen now, for you where it reads: "One member of the Skelani Platoon of the 2nd Special Police Detachment was killed in the fighting with the enemy." Now, apart from Krle or Krsto, as you called him, were there any other members from the Skelani Platoon killed during that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now if I now then read that line that he was killed in the fighting with the enemy, that does not reflect what you learned about the way in which he died, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you consider that if someone is kept prisoner, grabs the weapon of one of the persons guarding him and shooting him, you consider that to be -- to be killed in the fighting with the enemy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Even if those persons are civilians, those who are kept there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I haven't understood you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, do you consider fighting with the enemy also any conflict arising in a detention situation with one of the detained civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. That would not be it. Killed in combat would mean that there was an exchange of fire, in my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was not the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will go back to this document later, precisely in the way you indicated now, and then I will tender it. Can we now look at P1147.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I may, just one quick point, Your Honour. The document that my colleague Mr. Stojanovic has been using is, I believe, identical to what has been admitted already under P00724. So that may obviate the necessity of tendering that document and may ease references to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a look at it. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Once more can we have P1147? This is the Srebrenica trial video. And can we see the time sequence from 25.53 to 26.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Was it possible for you to hear what the participants in this conversation said?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Just the -- a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we replay it? It's a very brief clip. Please direct your attention to what is being said and the road. So we need from 25.53 to 26.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is my first question: Two names are mentioned here, Oficir and Bor. Can you tell us, do you know who was called Oficir from those participated in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Oficir is the nickname --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Probably the sixth time that we are focusing on what is Oficir. So therefore if you want to do it the seventh time, it's your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. I only wanted to have it said for the sake of this radio conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So Rade Cuturic is Oficir?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who had the code name of Bor for the purposes of communication?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Bor was the name for the deputy commander of our brigade, Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to recognise the voice of the individual saying that traffic should be stopped?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. It's not familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P1132 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, could we perhaps not with the level of sound as we have, could we play this same few seconds?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We hear of a third name, Todor. Is that a name familiar to you, apart from Bor and Oficir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: While you still have this image in front of you, can you tell us if you recognise the area and the road along which this vehicle is travelling?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. It might be a stretch of the road between Bratunac and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P1132 in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is from the Jean-Rene Ruez collection, as we refer to it, and could we please look at page 94 in e-court? Sir, please look at the image. Does this area and this building located in the red square seem to you that it could be the Kravica warehouse and the Sandici-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this building to the left of the road in the central, lower part of the building, look to you like the building that was close to the Sandici meadow which you said you know where it was?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And I'm going to finish with a question, if the buildings and houses in the central area of the photograph, to the left of the Kravica warehouse, could be the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please now, with the assistance of the usher, mark in this photograph the location where you were at the point in time when Rade Cuturic drove you to the feature that you refer to as Zuti Most, Yellow Bridge? Could you please mark the area where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was approximately here, on this part of the road. There was a kind of reinforcing wall. I can't see it here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, it's a little bit a difficult question to ask someone where he was when he was driven to a certain point, because it's inherent to being driven somewhere that you are not at one spot. Or did you intend to ask the witness where he was before he was driven to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honours. "Before," I did not say the word "before." So before he boarded Rade Cuturic's vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the place that you marked now?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell the Trial Chamber in your best recollection how far this is from the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Perhaps about 1 kilometre, a thousand metres. Perhaps more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you can approximately see that on this photograph, are you able to mark with a circle the place where, in your best recollection, Zuti Most was; i.e. where you got out of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yellow Bridge or Zuti Most, is in the very centre of Kravica village. Perhaps it's approximately here. Or perhaps a bit farther, higher in the image, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell the Trial Chamber in your best recollection how far this Yellow Bridge is from the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: About 8-, 900 metres, 1 kilometre, in my estimate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put ZM here the next this circle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Oh, you mean next to the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the transcript, the circle that is below the red square on this photograph is the area that the witness indicated was the area where he was before he got into Rade Cuturic's vehicle. Thank you. And, Your Honours, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document marked by the witness receives number D305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And one more question, Mr. Pepic. From the place where you were, that you call Zuti Most, is it possible visually to see the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, the upper part of it, the roof, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And at any point in time, while you were waiting for the order to halt traffic, were you able to see any movements of prisoners along the road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please tell the Trial Chamber - returning to the chronology of events - how long after you heard more intensive firing that was coming from the direction of the warehouse, did Rade Cuturic pass by you in his vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how much time passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And by that time, did you already stop the traffic and the vehicles along that road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Rade Cuturic alone in the vehicle that came past you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I remember that his hands were wrapped in bandages but I don't remember if he was by himself or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how long the conversation between you lasted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was very short. He was rushing off to the medical centre. He didn't stay long.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't issue any new instructions to you about letting traffic pass or not pass along the road?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He told you that there was firing on the Muslims or Muslims were being fired upon. Did he say anything else except that, perhaps regarding the place where this was happening?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. All he said was that there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to your statement, sometime later, about an hour later, Rade Cuturic came back. Is that a good estimate of time still today when you're testifying?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And for that entire hour, was shooting heard from that direction?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did the intensity of the shooting change or was it continuous?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It would change, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time, while you were on the bridge, after Rade Cuturic passed, did you see any other vehicle that was coming from the direction of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the way back, did Rade Cuturic in any way say anything to you as he passed by you on Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. All he said was to stay there until he tells me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long after he passed by did you receive a new order to let the traffic pass?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how much time passed, but it was very soon after, if I remember correctly. I cannot remember the precise time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After he passed by you on his way back to Sandici and Kravica again, at one point in time did the shooting stop?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After you let the traffic through, how long did you then stay at this place that you call Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Not long. Our bus came by, I boarded the bus, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And other than you, was there anybody else assigned to that task given to you by Rade Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't see any military formations there next to you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And now this is something that is confusing me the whole time. This bus that you boarded, which direction did it come from?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It came from the direction of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know actually where the bus was before all of these events?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know whether it was in Bratunac or if it was closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the driver of the bus?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There were a number of them. I don't remember exactly which driver it was then. We had several drivers. I don't know who was driving then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At the point in time when he came to Zuti Most in the village of Kravica and you boarded the bus, were there any other members of your detachment, the Sekovici detachment, on the bus?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You described passing by the Kravica warehouse. What I want to ask you now is this: At the time, did you see any persons in military uniforms or in police uniforms in front of the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know. No, I don't remember. There were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it already beginning to get dark?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't stay long, you just passed by in your bus?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And where did the bus stop to pick up the other members of the 2nd Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: In Sandici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to the meadow that you talked about and said you knew where it was, was it from the direction that you were coming in on the bus? Was it before the Sandici meadow or after the Sandici meadow, on the way to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was at the elevation in Sandici. Then the meadow would be to the right of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, did you see if there were any prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't see -- I don't remember seeing any, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I have to ask you this because of other witnesses who will be coming: Are you able to tell us now if you paid any attention at all to whether there were any prisoners or anyone on the Sandici meadow or not?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't paying attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, would you allow me to put one additional question to the witness. Witness, you were asked by Mr. Stojanovic: "... did you see any persons in military uniforms or in police uniforms in front of the Kravica warehouse?" And your answer was: "Yes, I did." Can you tell me, did you see military and police uniforms there, that means both types of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only noticed military uniforms in front of the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me whether at any point in time you received information that you were relieved by members of the Jahorina training centre at your positions?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you going to agree with me that they were in military camouflage uniforms at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing those uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that there were cases before the Bosnia-Herzegovina court where members of the Jahorina training centre were tried for events that we are discussing here now?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that you also appeared as a witness in those cases?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, I want to ask you this. At the point in time when members of your detachment, the 2nd Sekovici Detachment, were boarding the bus, did you notice any members of the 3rd Platoon, your 3rd Platoon that you called the Skelani Platoon boarding the bus together with you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that they were boarding the bus with us. They had their own separate vehicle. I don't recall them boarding our bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask you a little differently. The members of the Skelani Platoon or the 3rd Platoon, did you see them the following day in Konjevic Polje or were they in some other location because of the death of members of their unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't recall seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Which platoon of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment did Krsto also known as Krle belong to?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was the 3rd Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Next you headed in the direction of Konjevic Polje and Drinjaca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If the chronology is right the night between the 13th and 14th, where did you sleep, where were you billeted?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were billeted in abandoned Muslim houses in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if that night or on the following day, at any point you saw any prisoners in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, at which time during your stay in Konjevic Polje did Rade Cuturic come to see you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the evening. It was dark. That much I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: By that point, had you learned more about what had, in fact, happened in front of the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be referring to some other documents so I would kindly ask that we take our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will take the break now, but I first -- first of all, the witness can follow the usher. We will take a break of 20 minutes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what you had uploaded at 65 ter 04082 is an incomplete version with all kind of underlinings of what has been admitted into evidence as P00724. Therefore, there is no need to have it again in evidence. We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pepic, if you remember, we left for the break when we were discussing Konjevic Polje and the arrival of Rade Cuturic to the building where you were billeted. Can you now tell us in your own words to the best of your recollection what it was that Rade told you? How did that incident in front of the Kravica warehouse unfold?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: From what I remember, when he came he told us how Krle was killed. He happened to be in the midst of the Muslims who had surrendered. One of the Muslims grabbed his rifle from him and killed him. Oficir took the rifle by the barrel, and he burned his fist in the process, the palm of his hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before the rifle was seized and Krsto was killed, were any prisoners being killed? Did Rade tell you anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you what became of the body of late Krsto, aka Krle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what he said about what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if, at any point in time during your stay at the Yellow Bridge in Kravica, did a vehicle pass by which could have carried the body of Krle or Krsto?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not whether a vehicle passed by but whether it could have carried a body. Of course, every vehicle can carry a body. That's specific for vehicles, as a matter of fact, that they can carry persons, hidden or not hidden. Could you please ask focused and relevant questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to be more specific. Perhaps there was some problem with interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point during your presence at the Yellow Bridge, did you observe the arrival of a vehicle from the direction of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you are receiving some comments on your questions, and if you then say it is a translation problem, then I always want that to be substantiated because there is a risk -- I'm not saying you did -- but there is a risk that our good interpreters are blamed for whatever goes wrong in this courtroom, and that is something I would not accept for a second. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That is not my objective. Can we look at P1477 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I interrupted. Perhaps we first receive an answer to the question you put to the witness: "... did you observe the arrival of a vehicle from the direction of --" Mr. Stojanovic, which direction did you point at?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: From the direction of Kravica, after the departure of Rade Cuturic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to look at P1477. And I'd like to ask that it not be broadcast. Can we have the next page? Your Honour, this is a logbook of the health -- of a health centre. We were already looking that the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's look at the row numbered 1490, under date of wounding, can you see that, it's in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Under date of wounding it reads, 13 July 1994, at 1740 hours.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then, in the column first name, father's name, last name and rank, it reads, "Krsto," or rather, it reads, "Rade, son of Milan Cuturic." Would this time indicated here, i.e. 1740 hours, be consistent with your memory of when Rade Cuturic passed along the way where you were on his way to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, that could be the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell the Chamber, since you are familiar with the area, under ordinary circumstances, how long would it take to get from Kravica to the Bratunac health centre, going by car?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Some 30 to 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with all due respect, page 74, line 19, it says "30 to 40 minutes." I think the witness gave a different answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could you again tell us how much time it would take under normal circumstances to get from Kravica to the Bratunac health centre, by car? Could you repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 20 to 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the next column now, or actually, the next row, 1491? 13 July 1995, at 1900 hours, first and last name, Krsto, Dragicevic, son of Bogoljub. The time indicated here, 1900 hours, and in view of your earlier answer, would it reflect the time when he was harmed or when he arrived at the Bratunac health centre?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can I ask that this specific entry in the B/C/S version could be enlarged? That means the second column in relation to 1491. No, only the entry in the middle, yes, 1491. Could only the entry in the second column 1491 be enlarged? Thank you. Witness, would you consider this to be 1900 hours or is it a different one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It looks like a 9, 1900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. But would you agree that there was, before the 9 was written, another number beneath that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. One could say that there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at it more closely, now that it's enlarged, is it possible that number 8 was rewritten into 9?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, it could be an 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At any rate, now that you've seen this document, do you still stand by your position that at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, again, and again, the Defence has brought to our attention that every single word containing an opinion would be expertise. Well, the Chamber is relatively flexible on that. Now, is it the Defence's position that the 9 comes after the 8 or does it also allow for the possibility that the 8 comes after the 9? I mean, which was written first, which was written second? Is there -- that is really something that requires expert knowledge and opinion. What is now the position of the Defence, that it's both possible or -- apart from dealing with it with the witness, the witness apparently doesn't know anything about it and is invited to comment on what you see, what the Chamber sees and what the Prosecution sees, and what the witness sees. He's not in any position to judge better on this matter than anyone else. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would completely agree, Your Honours. The witness can only testify about what he heard and saw. And I'm interested in the time that is in the logbook in relation to what he heard and what he saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what you were asking him is to do something different, that is to interpret two numbers which are apparently the one over the other or the other way around. That's what you were asking the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to get an answer to my question whether you, sir, stand by what you said that when he was passing by, Rade Cuturic told you that Krle was killed?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you stand by what you said that Rade Cuturic passed by you at some point in time at approximately 1700 hours and 40 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you the following: According to your best recollection, how much time did you spend in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Till the afternoon perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So it would be good to conclude that you spent the night and then the following day in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So what was your next order?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The next order was that we were being sent to Zvornik, and then we were sent to the sector of Baljkovica. It's a place not far from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did members of the Jahorina training centre set off with you as well?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And members of the Jahorina training centre, at any point in time, were they together with you in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't say so. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: According to your best recollection, can you please tell us what sort of a unit are we talking about when we say the Jahorina training centre unit?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to say. They were members of the Special Police force. I don't know what kind of a training was meant. I really couldn't tell you anything about the unit, the status or the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time see along the road or at Zuti bridge in Potocari any units with canines?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if in July 1995 there was a canine police unit part of the MUP units that trained and used dogs?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which this unit -- what exactly -- which unit this was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: It was a unit located at Crepoljsko. It was a unit, I don't know the exact name of the unit but they were for the training, the use of dogs for official duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see this unit with dogs out in the field anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Who issued the order for you to set off towards Zvornik on the 14th in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Our commander, Rade Cuturic, Oficir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And did you stop off in Zvornik for any point in time before going to Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, because we continued on to the Baljkovica sector almost right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And was Rade Cuturic still on duty in view of the injuries that he had sustained?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he tell you at any point in time that he sustained the injuries from a rifle that was confiscated or seized from Krsto, aka Krle?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever have information about a person by the name of Miroslav Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at the document that you see in front of you, this is P1477. We will look at 1489, that entry of the 13th of July, 1995, at 1730 hours, Miroslav Stanojevic was wounded, a member of the Red Beret units n Kravica. What I want to ask you now is this? Can one reach Bratunac from the village of Kravica using some other road other than the asphalt road that passes along Yellow Bridge where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what route that would be?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: There is a macadam road up there, I don't know exactly, and you can go all the way down to this place. I don't know what -- what it's called. And then you can reach Zvornik -- no. You can reach Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say the village of Kravica, would you agree with me that this is a broader area that includes a number of hamlets?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the column of the 28th Division or a part of it passed right next to the village of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I heard that it did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you ever hear anything from Rade Cuturic about a person by the name of Miroslav Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At any point in time, did Rade Cuturic tell you anything about who was in front of the Kravica warehouse when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which incident are you referring to, Mr. -- the killing of Krle or the shooting or anything in relation to Mr. Stanojevic? What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I was not precise enough when I said incident. What I was referring to was the death of Krsto in that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how you understood the question and that's how you answered it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Before you left to go in the field to Baljkovica, did you at any point in time notice the return of the 3rd Platoon or the Skelani Platoon, as we refer to it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the platoon was allowed to go to the village of Skelani for the funeral?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: That's what happened most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: At one point you said that you stayed a little bit in Zvornik. So now I'm asking you: Can you remember actually where you were physically?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were around the old bridge, which is where the bus station is presently. But we stayed there very, very briefly and then we were sent on our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And Rade Cuturic, as your superior, was he with you at that time, or did he go off somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if he was with us the entire time, but he was with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know from whom Rade Cuturic received instructions which he conveyed to you, that you should go to Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, can you please tell us, what was the specific assignment that you received from Rade Cuturic when you were on the way to Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: The assignment was to send us to the village or the settlement of Baljkovica which is where the Serbian positions were, and to help them out, help out the Serbs on the positions, and to try to stop the Muslims that were trying to break through to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you told anything about the strength of the column that was moving towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO PEPIC
utterances.text: We were told that there was a large number of armed soldiers and that there was a large number of civilians together with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was hinting at the clock but I don't know whether you had any -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you're saying here at page 81 that you were sent to go and help some -- to help out the Serbs on the positions. What Serbs were these that you were helping, Serb civilians or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb soldiers, the Serb soldiers who were holding the positions around the location of Baljkovica, Serbian soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Serbian soldiers of which army? Serbian soldiers of which army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Serb army, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you were working in co-operation with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were sent to help them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, before we adjourn, Witness, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony or communicate in whatever other way with whomever, whether that's testimony already given or still to be given. We would like see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this same courtroom. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you tell us where you are in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think up to half an hour more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, I conferred with my colleagues, and a moderate assessment of 60 per cent of the questions where we really do not know what the relevance is, should have resulted in already having finished the cross-examination of this witness today. Nevertheless, you'll have another half an hour tomorrow, but please keep in mind that if you put questions to the witness of which we do not know what the relevance is, that it is most likely not supporting the Defence case. We adjourn for the day and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 11th of June at 9.30 in this same Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of June 2013, at 9.30 a.m. 25
